accepted_examples.german: Das Flugzeug flog um halb drei ab.
accepted_examples.note: The German sentence uses Flugzeug as the ordinary noun for an aircraft, and the translation matches the take-off event and time.

accepted_examples.german: Du musst aufhören, in der Vergangenheit zu leben.
accepted_examples.english: You have to stop living in the past.
accepted_examples.note: Vergangenheit means the past; the idiom in der Vergangenheit leben matches the English meaning.

accepted_examples.german: Boston ist wie eine zweite Heimat für mich.
accepted_examples.english: Boston is like my second home.
accepted_examples.note: zweite is the inflected form of second modifying Heimat, with the same meaning in English.

accepted_examples.german: Die Stadt wurde von einer großen Armee verteidigt.
accepted_examples.english: The town was defended by a large army.
accepted_examples.note: Armee means army in this sentence; the English translation preserves the defended-town context.

accepted_examples.english: I want to drink some hot tea.
accepted_examples.note: Tee means tea in a natural food-and-drink context, and heißen corresponds to hot.

accepted_examples.german: Glaubst du, ich ließe mich davon aufhalten?
accepted_examples.english: Do you think I'd let that stop me?
accepted_examples.note: aufhalten means stop or hold back here; the English translation expresses the same sense.

accepted_examples.german: Du musst dein Zimmer jeden Tag sauber machen.
accepted_examples.english: You must clean your room every day.
accepted_examples.note: sauber machen means clean/tidy in this everyday room-cleaning context.

accepted_examples.german: Ich versetzte ihm einen Schlag aufs Ohr.
accepted_examples.english: I dealt him a blow on the ear.
accepted_examples.note: Schlag means a blow in the physical sense, matching the English translation.

accepted_examples.german: Der Sheriff erwartet dich in seinem Büro.
accepted_examples.english: The sheriff is waiting for you in his office.
accepted_examples.note: Sheriff is used for the same public official as in English.

accepted_examples.german: Ich habe es getan, um überleben zu können.
accepted_examples.english: I did that in order to survive.
accepted_examples.note: überleben means survive, matching the purpose clause and English translation.

accepted_examples.german: Ich muss mir ein Büro mit Tom teilen.
accepted_examples.english: I have to share an office with Tom.
accepted_examples.note: teilen means share in the ordinary sense of sharing an office.

accepted_examples.german: Das ist das größte Gebäude in der Stadt.
accepted_examples.english: It's the biggest building in the city.
accepted_examples.note: Gebäude means building; the comparative sentence and translation align.

accepted_examples.german: Er war bereit, sich seinem Schicksal zu stellen.
accepted_examples.english: He was ready to face his fate.
accepted_examples.note: Schicksal means fate/destiny in the idiom sich dem Schicksal stellen.

accepted_examples.german: Der Angeklagte erklärte dem Richter, unschuldig zu sein.
accepted_examples.english: The accused told the judge that he was innocent.
accepted_examples.note: Richter means judge in the legal context, with the dative recipient matching the translation.

accepted_examples.german: Ich bin besorgt, was wohl passiert, wenn Tom nicht gewinnt.
accepted_examples.english: I'm worried about what'll happen if Tom doesn't win.
accepted_examples.note: besorgt means worried, and the subordinate clause gives a plausible cause for concern.

accepted_examples.german: Die Küche in dem Haus ist sehr schön.
accepted_examples.english: The kitchen in that house is very nice.
accepted_examples.note: Küche means kitchen; the sentence and translation describe the same room.

accepted_examples.german: Das Volk lehnte sich gegen den König auf.
accepted_examples.english: The people rebelled against the king.
accepted_examples.note: Volk means a people/population as a collective, matching the rebellion context.

accepted_examples.german: Eines Tages werden wir die Wahrheit herausfinden.
accepted_examples.english: We'll discover the truth one day.
accepted_examples.note: herausfinden means find out/discover, and the truth is the object of that discovery.

held_examples.german: Tom ist entweder ein Döskopp oder ein Genie.
held_examples.reason: Döskopp is a strongly regional/colloquial insult, so this sentence is not a clear beginner-friendly example of the either-or conjunction.

held_examples.german: Sei bei ihm vorsichtig! Er ist ein Don Juan.
held_examples.reason: Don Juan is a fixed proper-name expression and does not demonstrate Don as an honorific title.

held_examples.german: Ihr plötzlicher Tod hat uns sehr überrascht.
held_examples.reason: The example centers on a sudden death, an unnecessarily distressing context for a general learner example.

held_examples.german: Was ist dein Lieblingszitat von Mark Twain?
held_examples.reason: Mark is only part of the proper name Mark Twain here; the sentence does not demonstrate the marrow sense.
The sentence uses Untertitel in the film-caption sense, while this entry’s selected meaning is subheading.

held_examples.german: Das Hemd ganz bis an den Hals zuknöpfen!
held_examples.reason: The source is an infinitive-style instruction fragment rather than a complete contextual sentence.

held_examples.german: Da die Königin kam, hissten sie die Flagge.
held_examples.reason: The German sentence and its English translation describe different events, so they are not a reliable bilingual pair.

editorial_examples.german: Du kannst entweder Tee oder Kaffee trinken.
editorial_examples.english: You can drink either tea or coffee.
editorial_examples.note: A short, neutral example that clearly demonstrates the correlative conjunction entweder ... oder.

editorial_examples.german: Don Miguel begrüßte die Gäste im Innenhof.
editorial_examples.english: Don Miguel welcomed the guests in the courtyard.
editorial_examples.note: Don is used as the honorific before a personal name, rather than as part of the fixed name Don Juan.

editorial_examples.german: Das Ergebnis hat uns alle überrascht.
editorial_examples.note: A neutral everyday example that directly expresses surprise.

editorial_examples.german: Das Mark im Inneren des Knochens bildet neue Blutzellen.
editorial_examples.english: The marrow inside the bone produces new blood cells.
editorial_examples.note: The sentence demonstrates Mark in the marrow sense, not the proper name Mark.

editorial_examples.german: Der Untertitel erklärt das Thema des Kapitels.
editorial_examples.english: The subheading explains the topic of the chapter.
editorial_examples.note: This uses Untertitel in the selected subheading sense.

editorial_examples.german: Ein warmer Schal schützt den Hals vor der Kälte.
editorial_examples.english: A warm scarf protects the neck from the cold.
editorial_examples.note: A complete, neutral sentence that demonstrates Hals as the body part.

editorial_examples.german: Die Königin empfing die Gäste im Schloss.
editorial_examples.english: The queen received the guests at the castle.
editorial_examples.note: A simple sentence with a direct translation and no unexplained flag-raising context.
